[**Drill section**]{.fam-badge} · This is the practice hub: one page per drillable artefact — the **Spring-2025 take-home exam** (catalogued as a lens, never solved) and the **six course exercises**. Each page works the method idioms in context. Use the **filters below** to find a drill by **method family** (linear / tree / unsupervised / neural / cross-cutting), by **type** (exam vs exercise), or by **dataset**. Every tag here is taken straight from that drill's extract — the exam's structure from `phase0/exam_spring2025_notebook.md`, each exercise's methods and dataset from its `phase0/exercise_0N_*.md` — so a tag means the drill *actually* uses that method on that data; nothing is invented. For the order in which to work them and which method pages to read first, see the [exercise dependency map](../cross_method/exercise_dependency_map.qmd).

::: {.callout-bigpicture}
**New here? Don't pick at random — follow the path.** The [exercise dependency map](../cross_method/exercise_dependency_map.qmd) lays out the suggested study order (1 → 6): preprocessing first ([Titanic](exercise_01_titanic_preprocessing.qmd)), then a from-scratch classifier ([spam / naive Bayes](exercise_02_spam_naive_bayes.qmd)), regression with shrinkage ([house prices](exercise_03_house_prices.qmd)), a multiclass bake-off ([MNIST digits](exercise_04_mnist_digits.qmd)), the evaluation toolkit ([model selection](exercise_05_model_selection.qmd)), and finally unsupervised segmentation ([customer segmentation](exercise_06_customer_segmentation.qmd)). The filter on this page is for *finding* a drill; that map is for *sequencing* them.
:::

::: {.callout-exam}
**The one drill that mirrors the real thing.** The [Spring-2025 exam drill](exam_spring2025.qmd) walks the representative 30-hour take-home format — four assignments (regularized regression on Hitters, clustering on WholesaleCustomers, ensembles on WDBC, a classification challenge on SimulatedData) — as a *lens* on how the methods are examined, never as solved answers. Read it to see which method pages each assignment leans on and how the pipeline-style workflow (load → EDA → encode/scale → split → tune via CV → evaluate → compare → interpret) recurs across all four (`phase0/exam_spring2025_notebook.md`).
:::

## Find a drill

Pick a **type**, **family**, and **dataset** to narrow the list. "Any" leaves that filter open. The family colors match the rest of the site ([linear]{style="color:var(--family-linear);font-weight:600"} · [tree]{style="color:var(--family-tree);font-weight:600"} · [unsupervised]{style="color:var(--family-unsup);font-weight:600"} · [neural]{style="color:var(--family-neural);font-weight:600"} · [cross-cutting]{style="color:var(--family-cross);font-weight:600"}). A drill can belong to more than one family; it matches a family filter if *any* of its families fits. If the interactive panel doesn't load, the [full static table below](#sec-drill-table) lists the same items, tags, and links.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| label: drill-filter

// --- family colors, read from the page CSS vars (fallbacks per theme/custom.scss) ---
famLinear = (getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--family-linear').trim() || "#2E86AB")
famTree   = (getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--family-tree').trim()   || "#06A77D")
famUnsup  = (getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--family-unsup').trim()  || "#F18F01")
famNeural = (getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--family-neural').trim() || "#7B2CBF")
famCross  = (getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--family-cross').trim()  || "#3D405B")

famColor = ({linear: famLinear, tree: famTree, unsup: famUnsup, neural: famNeural, cross: famCross})
famLabel = ({linear: "linear", tree: "tree", unsup: "unsupervised", neural: "neural", cross: "cross-cutting"})

// --- drill items: every field traced to phase0 extracts (no network — inline, C8) ---
//   type:     "exam" | "exercise"
//   families: method-family tags (a drill can carry several)
//   datasets: dataset(s) the drill's solution actually uses
//   methods:  short list of methods exercised (for the row blurb)
//   href:     relative link to the drill page (same folder)
drills = [
  {
    n: "Exam", title: "Spring-2025 take-home exam", href: "exam_spring2025.qmd",
    type: "exam",
    families: ["linear", "unsup", "tree", "cross"],
    datasets: ["Hitters", "WholesaleCustomers", "wdbc", "SimulatedData"],
    methods: "OLS / Ridge / Lasso · PCA + K-means · Decision Tree / Random Forest / Gradient Boosting · CV tuning + classification challenge",
    note: "4 assignments; catalogued as a lens, not solved"
  },
  {
    n: "01", title: "Titanic preprocessing", href: "exercise_01_titanic_preprocessing.qmd",
    type: "exercise",
    families: ["cross"],
    datasets: ["Titanic"],
    methods: "Missing-value imputation, outlier handling, categorical encoding, conditional survival probabilities — preprocessing / EDA only, no estimator",
    note: "foundational; no model fitted"
  },
  {
    n: "02", title: "Spam filtering — naive Bayes", href: "exercise_02_spam_naive_bayes.qmd",
    type: "exercise",
    families: ["cross"],
    datasets: ["SMSSpam"],
    methods: "Multinomial naive Bayes from scratch + sklearn MultinomialNB, CountVectorizer bag-of-words",
    note: "naive Bayes is drill-only (no method page); dataset [DATA-1] missing"
  },
  {
    n: "03", title: "House prices", href: "exercise_03_house_prices.qmd",
    type: "exercise",
    families: ["linear"],
    datasets: ["house-prices"],
    methods: "OLS baseline, Ridge, Lasso; Lasso feature-selection (SelectFromModel); in/out-of-sample MSE & R²",
    note: "the Assignment-1 regression skill"
  },
  {
    n: "04", title: "MNIST digits", href: "exercise_04_mnist_digits.qmd",
    type: "exercise",
    families: ["linear", "tree"],
    datasets: ["digits"],
    methods: "Multinomial logistic baseline, kNN, Decision Tree, naive Bayes, SVM; manual max_depth / n_neighbors sweeps",
    note: "multiclass model bake-off"
  },
  {
    n: "05", title: "Model selection & evaluation", href: "exercise_05_model_selection.qmd",
    type: "exercise",
    families: ["cross"],
    datasets: ["iris"],
    methods: "cross_val_score, GridSearchCV, confusion matrices across kNN / Decision Tree / Logistic / SVM; ROC/PR discussion",
    note: "the evaluation toolkit"
  },
  {
    n: "06", title: "Customer segmentation", href: "exercise_06_customer_segmentation.qmd",
    type: "exercise",
    families: ["unsup"],
    datasets: ["bank"],
    methods: "K-means (elbow WCSS + silhouette), PCA 2D viz, StandardScaler + one-hot encoding",
    note: "only unsupervised exercise; dataset [DATA-2] missing"
  }
]

// --- filter option lists, derived from the data ---
allDatasets = Array.from(new Set(drills.flatMap(d => d.datasets))).sort()
allFamilies = ["linear", "tree", "unsup", "neural", "cross"]   // canonical order

// --- the three Inputs ---
viewof typeSel = Inputs.radio(
  new Map([["Any type", "any"], ["Exam", "exam"], ["Exercise", "exercise"]]),
  {label: "Type", value: "any"}
)
viewof familySel = Inputs.select(
  new Map([["Any family", "any"], ...allFamilies.map(f => [famLabel[f], f])]),
  {label: "Method family", value: "any"}
)
viewof datasetSel = Inputs.select(
  ["any", ...allDatasets],
  {label: "Dataset", value: "any", format: d => d === "any" ? "Any dataset" : d}
)

// --- reactive filtered list ---
filtered = drills.filter(d =>
  (typeSel    === "any" || d.type === typeSel) &&
  (familySel  === "any" || d.families.includes(familySel)) &&
  (datasetSel === "any" || d.datasets.includes(datasetSel))
)

// --- render: a count line + one card per matching drill ---
html`<div style="margin:.4rem 0 .8rem;font-size:.9rem;color:#666">
  Showing <strong>${filtered.length}</strong> of ${drills.length} drills.
</div>`

html`<div style="display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:.55rem">
  ${filtered.length === 0
    ? html`<div style="padding:.8rem;border:1px dashed #ccc;border-radius:8px;color:#777">No drill matches that combination. Reset a filter to "Any".</div>`
    : filtered.map(d => html`
      <div style="border:1px solid #e3e3e3;border-left:4px solid ${famColor[d.families[0]]};border-radius:8px;padding:.6rem .8rem">
        <div style="display:flex;align-items:baseline;gap:.5rem;flex-wrap:wrap">
          <span style="font-size:.72rem;font-weight:700;color:#fff;background:${d.type === "exam" ? famCross : "#888"};border-radius:4px;padding:.05rem .4rem;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.03em">${d.type}</span>
          <a href="${d.href}" style="font-weight:700;font-size:1.02rem;text-decoration:none">${d.n === "Exam" ? "" : d.n + " · "}${d.title}</a>
        </div>
        <div style="margin:.35rem 0 .3rem">
          ${d.families.map(f => html`<span style="display:inline-block;font-size:.72rem;font-weight:600;color:#fff;background:${famColor[f]};border-radius:4px;padding:.05rem .45rem;margin-right:.3rem">${famLabel[f]}</span>`)}
          ${d.datasets.map(ds => html`<span style="display:inline-block;font-size:.72rem;color:#555;background:#f0f0f2;border:1px solid #ddd;border-radius:4px;padding:.05rem .45rem;margin-right:.3rem">${ds}</span>`)}
        </div>
        <div style="font-size:.85rem;color:#444;line-height:1.4">${d.methods}</div>
        ${d.note ? html`<div style="font-size:.78rem;color:#888;margin-top:.25rem;font-style:italic">${d.note}</div>` : ""}
      </div>`)}
</div>`
```

: The seven drills — type, method family, dataset, and focus. Tags trace to the `phase0` extracts. {.striped tbl-colwidths="[24,9,17,22,28]"}

::: {.callout-note}
**Two drills depend on datasets not present in the repo.** Exercise 02 (spam) needs the **SMS Spam Collection** (`[DATA-1]` — the solution loads `data/smsspamcollection/SMSSpamCollection.csv`, absent locally) and exercise 06 (segmentation) needs the **UCI Bank Marketing** file (`[DATA-2]` — `data/bank_marketing_data_set/.../bank-additional-full.csv`, also absent). Both drill pages are written from the VHL solution extracts, but the code blocks won't *run* until those files are supplied. Everything else (Titanic, house-prices, and the sklearn built-ins `digits`/`iris`) is available or self-contained.
:::

## Where to go next

- **In what order should I work these?** → the [exercise dependency map](../cross_method/exercise_dependency_map.qmd) gives the 1 → 6 study path and the prerequisite method pages for each.
- **I want to drill toward the exam.** → start at the [Spring-2025 exam drill](exam_spring2025.qmd); each assignment names the method pages it tests.
- **Where do methods compete on shared data?** → the [Showdowns](../cross_method/showdowns.qmd) page (e.g. OLS vs Ridge vs Lasso vs Tree vs RF on Hitters), and the [Decision Dashboard](../cross_method/decision_dashboard.qmd) for choosing among them.
